top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level firmware-visible controller integrating MMIO register decode, DoMINO surrogate control, safety gating, fault latching, and SRAM-backed history telemetry. It emits external model-request transport outputs, receives model-response transport inputs, and bounds actuator validity/data without any fallback command behavior.
top_module.functionality: Integrates software control, surrogate-model transport, safety gating, and history memory into a single synthesizable top. The module accepts MMIO transactions, exposes software-visible configuration and status, issues model requests, consumes model responses, validates freshness and operating range, and produces bounded actuator commands only when all conditions are satisfied. It also exposes model transport handshakes, debug telemetry, and an SRAM macro interface for bulk history storage. On invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions, the design inhibits actuator command validity and latches the fault for firmware handling; it does not generate any substitute command.
responsibilities: Expose a real firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface with address, write-data, read-data, valid, write-enable, and ready semantics.
Drive the external model-request transport outputs and consume the model-response transport inputs with the specified directionality.
Provide bounded actuator command output only when the control and safety conditions are met.
Latch faults and inhibit validity on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or unsafe conditions.
Map bulk telemetry/history storage onto a technology-neutral SRAM macro interface.
Keep all software-visible registers reachable through RTL decode.
Preserve the DoMINO-based surrogate partition and transparent reference behavior without introducing fallback behavior.
top_module.reset_behavior: On synchronous reset assertion, all output-valid signals are deasserted, command data is driven to a safe zero-valued inactive state, MMIO ready returns to an idle-safe state, model request and model response handshake outputs are inactive, memory write access is disabled, and the fault latch is cleared or held according to the implemented latch policy without generating any fallback command. After reset, the controller remains inhibited until software enables operation through MMIO and the runtime conditions are valid.
behavior_rules: The top module shall only assert actuator_cmd_valid when control enable is active, the aircraft state is valid, the vehicle speed is within 20 to 55 m/s inclusive, the model response is valid and fresh, and no fault is latched.
If the model response does not arrive before the configured timeout threshold, the design shall latch a fault and deassert actuator_cmd_valid.
If response age exceeds the configured stale threshold, the design shall latch a fault and deassert actuator_cmd_valid.
The model-request transport shall emit valid/data only when the controller is enabled and not faulted.
The model-response ready output shall be asserted only when the controller is prepared to consume a response.
No fallback command, fallback register, substitute command, or fallback-on-reset behavior is permitted; the design must inhibit validity instead.
The debug trace and history storage may record request/response/command/fault events but may not replace the externally requested command.
The SRAM-backed history store shall capture bulk history without flattening it into registers.

modules.name: register_bank_mmio
modules.description: Firmware-visible register bank and MMIO decode block. It implements the declared registers, exposes semantic configuration and status signals to the controller, and provides readable status and telemetry mirrors. This module is the sole decode point for software-visible registers and does not implement any substitute command path.
modules.functionality: Implements all software-visible control and status registers for the adaptive aerodynamics controller. It decodes MMIO transactions, provides ready/read-data response, and exposes semantic outputs that configure the controller and reflect live status. The register bank controls enabling, override permission, request gating, timeout and stale thresholds, command bounds, and speed bounds for 20–55 m/s operation. It mirrors selected status fields from the controller but never supplies a substitute command path.
responsibilities: Decode every declared software-visible register through RTL logic.
Provide read and write semantics for control, threshold, and status registers.
Expose semantic configuration outputs to the controller as real ports.
Mirror fault, timeout, stale, speed, and command telemetry for firmware.
Never hide internal state as software-visible if it is not reachable through decode.
Preserve bounded-control configuration and the explicit operating-speed range.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, control and request enables deassert, thresholds and bounds return to safe defaults consistent with the 20–55 m/s contract, and status mirrors clear or hold according to the implemented fault policy. MMIO response is idle-safe during reset. No fallback command is generated or written into status.
behavior_rules: Every implemented register must be reachable through MMIO decode.
Status mirrors shall reflect controller-observed conditions only and shall not be used as substitute control inputs.
Software-visible fields shall include enable, override, request gating, timeout threshold, stale threshold, command bounds, and speed bounds.
Fault and telemetry mirrors shall be readable and updated consistently with controller observation.
The register bank shall not implement any hidden actuator fallback or substitute command mechanism.

modules.name: domino_surrogate_controller
modules.description: Physics-based surrogate interface and control partition built around NVIDIA DoMINO as the active-aerodynamics physics surrogate. This block forms the transparent reference and partitioned inference path: it consumes semantic requests and state, emits model requests, consumes model responses, validates them against confidence and range checks, and produces candidate aerodynamic command estimates and trace words. It does not directly drive the actuator output and it does not invent fallback control.
modules.functionality: Implements the DoMINO surrogate-based control partition. It generates model requests from the current vehicle state and configuration, waits for model responses, validates response freshness, and computes a candidate command estimate constrained to the configured command range. This module provides the transparent reference and partition boundary for the active-aerodynamics architecture. It reports timeout and stale-data events but never substitutes a fallback command.
responsibilities: Form model requests for the surrogate using the semantic vehicle state and control configuration.
Consume model responses with explicit ready/valid transport semantics.
Validate output freshness, range, and candidate-command boundedness.
Emit candidate control only when the surrogate response is usable.
Provide trace/debug information for verification and firmware observability.
Report timeout and stale events to the top-level safety manager.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, request and candidate outputs are inactive, model response ready is deasserted until control is enabled, and timeout/stale events are cleared. No fallback command is produced. Debug trace output is inactive or zeroed.
behavior_rules: The candidate command must remain within the provided command_min to command_max bounds.
If control_enable or request_enable is low, no request shall be issued and candidate_valid shall remain low.
If model response is invalid or absent beyond the programmed timeout, timeout_event shall assert.
If a response is too old relative to the stale threshold, stale_event shall assert.
Pilot override may affect the candidate path only if it is enabled upstream by configuration; otherwise it is ignored.
The surrogate path is the DoMINO-based physics-based estimator; it is not a substitute fallback controller.

modules.name: safety_manager
modules.description: Safety, timeout, stale-data, operating-range, and fault-latch manager. It consumes candidate commands and controller state, inhibits actuator validity on invalid conditions, and latches faults for firmware handling. The safety manager is intentionally strict and never produces a fallback command; it only passes bounded commands when all conditions are satisfied.
modules.functionality: Implements the final gating and safety decision. It checks configured speed range, candidate validity, timeout and stale conditions, and any explicit fault-clear control. It latches faults for software handling and inhibits actuator output validity whenever the command would be invalid, stale, timed out, out of range, or otherwise unsafe. It forwards a bounded command only when all gating conditions are satisfied. No fallback command or substitute controller output is ever emitted.
responsibilities: Latch faults on invalid, stale, timeout, out-of-range, or reset-induced unsafe conditions according to policy.
Inhibit actuator_cmd_valid whenever the command cannot be proven safe.
Forward only bounded commands that have passed validation.
Report last speed and last command for status visibility.
Expose model-timeout and stale-data indicators to software.
Never create fallback-on-reset or substitute-command behavior.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, actuator_cmd_valid is deasserted, actuator_cmd is held inactive or zero, and fault_latched is set or cleared only according to the implemented latch policy without generating any fallback command. Timeout and stale indicators are cleared or deasserted at reset entry. Software-visible status registers reflect the reset state after synchronization.
behavior_rules: The actuator command output is valid only when candidate_valid is high, no timeout/stale/fault condition exists, aircraft_state_valid is high, and vehicle_speed_mps lies within the configured range.
If fault_clear is asserted and the underlying unsafe condition is absent, the fault latch may be cleared; otherwise it remains latched.
The module shall not synthesize a substitute command when candidate_valid is low or when any fault condition is present.
Status mirrors must reflect the most recent safe observed command and speed.
The command output must always remain bounded by command_min and command_max when valid.

modules.name: history_telemetry_buffer
modules.description: SRAM-backed bulk history and telemetry buffer wrapper. Stores recent request, response, command, and fault trace entries in technology-neutral block RAM mapped through the declared memory macro. It exists to preserve history without flattening bulk storage into registers.
modules.functionality: Captures recent telemetry and trace words into the SRAM macro and supports readback of buffered history for verification and firmware debug. The buffer uses the external memory macro defined in memory_macros and does not create a register-array substitute. It records model-request, model-response, command, and fault trace words supplied by the top-level integration path.
responsibilities: Write bulk history entries into block RAM.
Provide a readback path for firmware or debug consumers.
Consume the physical memory macro dout as a real input and expose read data for the controller path.
Avoid flattening the history into registers.
Support technology mapping to native block RAM or external macro collateral.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, memory access is deasserted inactive, history_valid is low, and any internal write pointers or counters return to their reset state. The macro contents are not overwritten by a fallback pattern; reads after reset follow the macro's native contents and the controller's safe access policy.
behavior_rules: Bulk history must reside in the technology-neutral memory macro, not in registers.
The memory dout input from the macro must be consumed by the wrapper and/or top-level path.
The buffer shall record trace words corresponding to request, response, command, and fault events.
No substitute command or fallback telemetry shall be written into history on fault.
